strip.label: Built around the systems you already use:

partner.label: Local Expertise
paragraphs: ERP integration isn’t just about connecting APIs – it’s about understanding business processes and making systems work together seamlessly. Every setup is different, and the challenges usually hide in the details: in how orders, stock and invoices really move through the business.

The key is clear requirements, proper data ownership, and testing with real-world scenarios. Our approach ensures the integration becomes a reliable part of your daily operations, not a source of constant firefighting.

reliable.label: Behind the integration
reliable.title: What makes an integration reliable
paragraphs: A reliable integration is more than connecting two systems. It means defining field mapping and data ownership, handling webhooks and API limits, and building in retries, reconciliation and monitoring so critical data keeps moving reliably across Shopify, ERP, POS and the rest of your infrastructure.

When an existing connector fits the process, we use it. When the business logic is more complex, we build the integration layer around it — based on the systems involved, data volume, operational risk and how the business actually works.

case.label: Proven in practice
challenge: Fresh Market sells the same inventory through its Shopify store and physical locations. Without a shared inventory flow, an item sold in-store could remain available online — creating overselling, cancelled orders and manual stock corrections.
The challenge was to make both channels operate against the same inventory, so every sale is reflected across the business automatically.
built: We built a connected commerce system that keeps the online store, physical locations and inventory in sync through a custom integration layer. A private app handles the business-specific logic, while automated data flows keep stock availability updated across channels as sales happen.
Instead of managing online and offline inventory separately, the store operates around one connected flow — with Shopify, POS and inventory data working together behind the scenes.

process.label: Our Process
process.title:
From mapping the complexity

steps.title: Map the System
steps.description: We map every system, workflow and dependency, and define what data each one owns before deciding how they should connect.

steps.title: Plan the Logic
steps.description: We define how data should move, what happens when systems disagree and where custom logic is needed before anything gets built.

steps.title: Build & Test
steps.description: We build the integration layer, apps and automations, then run real scenarios through them — including the ones that fail.

steps.title: Launch & Monitor
steps.description: We launch under real conditions and keep watching the critical flows, because integrations need to keep working after go-live.

items.q: Can you connect Shopify to our ERP?
items.a: Yes. Orders, stock levels and invoices move between Shopify and your ERP without anyone re-typing them. We work through the API your ERP exposes, and where it exposes nothing usable we build the connector ourselves rather than telling you it cannot be done.

items.q: What if our system has no Shopify app?
items.a: That is most of the work we do. Off-the-shelf apps cover common systems; the one that runs your business often predates them or was built in-house. We connect those directly through their API, or build a private Shopify app to sit between them.

items.q: How do you stop stock going out of sync?
items.a: By deciding which system owns the number before anything is built. Stock drifts when two systems both think they are authoritative, so we set direction and frequency for every field, then run real orders through it, including the ones that fail, before it touches live data.

items.q: Can you automate order routing and fulfilment?
items.a: Yes. For a UK gifting brand we built a production engine that turns each order into print-ready files, batches them and routes them to the production queue, plus a fulfilment layer that generates shipping codes, syncs couriers in real time and schedules pickups twice a day.

items.q: Which ERPs and CRMs have you worked with?
items.a: ERP, CRM, PIM and fulfilment systems across the common categories, connected through whatever API they expose. Several clients run systems with no public integration at all, and for those we have built custom connectors for the specific use rather than moving the business onto a different tool.

items.q: How long does an integration take?
items.a: It depends on how many systems and how clean their data is. A single well-documented connection is measured in weeks. The UK gifting brand's three-system build, covering configurator, production and fulfilment, took four to six months. We scope it before quoting.

We do, if you want us to. Integrations break when either side changes: an API version is deprecated, a field is renamed, a system is upgraded. We monitor and alert on the connections we build, because a silent integration failure costs more than a loud one.

items.q: Can you integrate with our warehouse or 3PL?
items.a: Yes. We have built barcode scanning and routing logic into warehouse operations, and courier integrations that generate labels, push tracking back to the store and schedule collections. Nova Poshta Connect is the public version of that work, listed on the Shopify App Store.
